newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to offer new flat long-distance rate.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to offer new flat long-distance rate.

text.p: AT&T said it is offering the industry's first single-rate, long-distance calling plan available 24 hours a day.

The largest U.S. long-distance telephone service provider said its new plan, One Rate, will allow consumers to make direct-dialed long-distance calls at any time to any location in the U.S. for a flat rate of $0.15 a minute.
Separately, AT&T in a second press release said its third quarter earnings could be as much as 10 percent below analysts mean estimate of $0.92 per share due to competitive pressures.
It said its Q3 results will be hurt by investments and competitive pressures and that fourth quarter estimates will also likely fall short of analysts' estimates of $0.89 per share.
AT&T said its One Rate plan has no enrollment fee and is available now. The plan comes at a time when rivals are making aggressive promotional offers and new competitors are entering long-distance.
AT&T said the plan contrasts with others in that other companies' offer low rates for only a portion of the day and can have spending minimums and other restrictions.
AT&T said it will hold a press briefing on the calling plan at 1015 EST via conference call.
